name: Bunnings
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Australia's largest home improvement and hardware chain, running 382 Bunnings warehouses across Australia and New Zealand.
capacity_detail: Revenue A$19.6bn in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox), about USD 12.7bn at 0.65
markets: Australia and New Zealand: 382 Bunnings stores plus Beaumont Tiles and Tool Kit Depot outlets
rationale: Mass-market DIY brand with a huge male, trade and family customer base that overlaps the Australian Grand Prix audience.

name: Jetstar
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Low-cost airline flying domestic and international routes across Australia, New Zealand and Asia, wholly owned by Qantas.
capacity_detail: Revenue A$5.711bn in 2024/25 (Wikipedia infobox), about USD 3.7bn at 0.65
sponsorships: Gold Coast Titans NRL major sponsor 2008-2012; official airline of Australian rugby league team (2008)
markets: Domestic Australia and New Zealand plus about 40 destinations across Asia-Pacific
rationale: Leisure-travel airline that could package fan travel to the Australian, Singapore and Japanese Grands Prix.

name: Optus
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Australia's second-largest telecommunications company, offering mobile, broadband and entertainment services, wholly owned by Singtel.
capacity_detail: Official partner of the Australian Olympic and Paralympic Teams under a 10-year deal from 2016 to 2026; revenue A$8.05bn (2023)
sponsorships: Australian Olympic Committee partner 2016-2026; Optus Stadium naming rights; Adelaide Crows (AFL); Collingwood AFLW; Supercars sponsor of Chaz Mostert
markets: Australia-wide mobile, broadband and streaming customers
rationale: Sports-heavy telco brand already sponsoring Olympics, AFL and Supercars; F1 content and the Melbourne race fit its streaming push.

name: Shopee
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Leading e-commerce marketplace in Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Brazil, operated by Singapore-based Sea Limited.
capacity_detail: Shopee GAAP revenue USD 16.6bn for full year 2025 (Sea results release)
markets: Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore), Taiwan, Brazil, cross-border Argentina
rationale: Mass-market consumer brand fighting Lazada and TikTok Shop; F1's Singapore race and young Asian fanbase suit its campaigns.

name: Garena
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Game developer and publisher behind Free Fire, publishing mobile titles across Southeast Asia, Latin America and beyond.
capacity_detail: Garena GAAP revenue USD 2.4bn and bookings USD 2.9bn for full year 2025 (Sea results release)
sponsorships: Free Fire World Series; Esports World Cup partner (2024)
markets: Free Fire in more than 130 countries; publishing in Southeast Asia, Taiwan, Latin America, Middle East and North Africa
rationale: Gaming brand with huge young audience in Brazil and Asia; F1 tie-ins mirror rival PUBG Mobile's existing F1 deal.

name: Monee
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Sea Limited's digital financial services arm offering e-wallets, payments and consumer credit across Southeast Asia and Brazil.
capacity_detail: Monee GAAP revenue USD 3.8bn for full year 2025 (Sea results release)
markets: Southeast Asian markets and Brazil, alongside the Shopee marketplace
rationale: Fast-growing fintech brand renamed from SeaMoney that needs awareness; fintech rivals use F1 to build trust.

name: Officeworks
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Australian retailer of stationery, office furniture, technology and print services, operating about 176 stores for Wesfarmers.
capacity_detail: Revenue A$3.57bn in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox), about USD 2.3bn at 0.65
markets: Australia, through stores and online
rationale: Domestic small-business and technology retailer; limited fit beyond an Australian Grand Prix activation.

name: The Good Guys
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Australian retailer of white goods, kitchen appliances and consumer electronics, owned by JB Hi-Fi since 2016.
capacity_detail: Revenue A$2.81bn in 2023 (Wikipedia infobox), about USD 1.8bn at 0.65
markets: Australia, about 107 stores and online
rationale: Electronics retailer selling TVs to sports viewers; an Australian Grand Prix tie-in could drive big-screen sales.

name: Big W
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Australian discount department store chain selling toys, apparel, homewares and entertainment through about 179 stores.
capacity_detail: Revenue A$4.716bn per Wikipedia infobox (2026), about USD 3.1bn at 0.65
markets: Australia, about 179 stores and online
rationale: Loss-making discount chain in turnaround; family audience fit but low budget for international sport.

name: Country Road Group
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Australian fashion group owning Country Road, Mimco, Trenery, Politix and Witchery, with about 630 stores.
ownership: subsidiary of Woolworths Holdings (South Africa), full ownership since 2014
capacity_detail: Revenue R12.57bn in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox), about USD 690M at 18.3 ZAR/USD
markets: Australia, New Zealand and South Africa (88 of 630 locations in South Africa)
rationale: Premium apparel brands like Politix could use F1 hospitality and menswear styling, though the group is loss-making.

name: Kawasaki Motors
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Maker of Kawasaki motorcycles, ATVs, utility vehicles, Jet Ski watercraft and general-purpose engines, wholly owned by Kawasaki Heavy Industries.
capacity_detail: Powersports & Engine segment revenue JPY 682.8bn in year to March 2026 (KHI results), about USD 4.6bn at 150
sponsorships: Factory WorldSBK team backing (Provec Racing from 2012); Monster Energy Kawasaki Team Green motocross
markets: Motorcycles, ATVs and watercraft sold worldwide, strongest in North America, Europe and Asia
rationale: Performance motorcycle brand with racing heritage; F1 visibility would reach motorsport fans who already ride rival Ducati and Honda bikes.

name: NTT Data
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Global IT services, consulting and outsourcing company, delisted in 2025 and now wholly owned by NTT.
ownership: subsidiary of NTT (Nippon Telegraph and Telephone)
capacity_detail: Revenue JPY 4.64tn (about USD 29.3bn) in year to March 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
sponsorships: IndyCar Series title sponsor from 2019; Chip Ganassi Racing from 2017; Arrow McLaren from 2023; McLaren F1 team from 2023 and F1 Academy from 2024 (not on current roster)
markets: Offices or subsidiaries in Japan, US, UK, Italy, India, China, Brazil, Australia, Southeast Asia and more
rationale: Long-time motorsport technology sponsor (IndyCar, McLaren); renewing an F1 data partnership would showcase its AI and IT services.

name: Scoot
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Low-cost airline of Singapore Airlines flying from Changi to destinations across Asia, Oceania and Europe.
capacity_detail: Revenue S$2,349M in 2025 (Wikipedia business trends table), about USD 1.76bn at 0.75
markets: Over 16 countries and 56 destinations from Singapore across Asia, Oceania and Europe
rationale: Budget airline that could fly fans to the Singapore Grand Prix, building on its parent's existing F1 partnership.

name: Toyota Kirloskar Motor
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Indian car manufacturer building and selling Toyota vehicles in India, 89% owned by Toyota Motor Corporation.
ownership: subsidiary of Toyota Motor Corporation (89%); Kirloskar Group holds 11%
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 71,038 crore (about USD 7.6bn) in FY2026 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: India, with production of 337,148 units in 2025
rationale: Toyota's Indian arm could use its parent's Haas F1 link to lift premium models in India's growing F1 fanbase.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (Haas (Toyota Gazoo Racing))

name: JioStar
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Indian media company formed by merging Star India and Viacom18, running TV channels and the JioHotstar streaming service.
ownership: subsidiary of Reliance Industries (16.34% direct plus 46.82% through Viacom18, 63.16% in total); Disney holds 36.84%
capacity_detail: Merger of Star India and Viacom18 valued the venture at USD 8.5bn (Feb 2024 deal, closed Nov 2024)
markets: India, with television channels and streaming for Indian audiences
rationale: India's dominant sports broadcaster; F1 media rights or co-promotion could grow its streaming audience among affluent viewers.

name: Jio-bp
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Indian fuel and mobility retailer running over 1,700 fuel outlets, a joint venture of Reliance and BP.
ownership: subsidiary of Reliance Industries (51%); BP holds 49%
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 63,840 crore (about USD 6.8bn) in 2026 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: India, over 1,700 retail fuel outlets plus EV charging
rationale: Fuel brand competing with state oil companies; BP and Castrol F1 links give a ready playbook for motorsport marketing in India.

name: Coca-Cola Beverages Africa
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Largest Coca-Cola bottler in Africa, serving over 840,000 customer outlets across 14 countries from 35 plants.
ownership: subsidiary of The Coca-Cola Company (66.5%); Gutsche Family Investments 33.5%; 75% being sold to Coca-Cola HBC (listed), closing expected end-2026
capacity_detail: Sale of a 75% controlling interest to Coca-Cola HBC agreed Oct 2025 valued CCBA at about R59.2bn (about USD 3.2bn)
markets: 14 African countries including South Africa, served through 35 bottling plants
rationale: Bottler marketing Coca-Cola brands across Africa; limited own-brand freedom makes a direct F1 deal unlikely.

name: Pelephone
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Israeli mobile phone operator with about 2.6 million subscribers, wholly owned by telecom group Bezeq.
capacity_detail: Revenue ILS 1.98bn in 2023 (Wikipedia infobox), about USD 535M at 3.7
markets: Israel, about 2.6 million mobile customers
rationale: Domestic Israeli carrier; F1 content offers could lift loyalty, but international sponsorship value is limited.

name: A.S. Watson
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: International health and beauty retailer running Watsons, Superdrug, Kruidvat, Savers and other chains in 31 markets.
ownership: subsidiary of CK Hutchison Holdings (just over 75%); Temasek holds 25%
capacity_detail: Retail division (A.S. Watson) total revenue HK$209,267M in 2025 (CK Hutchison annual report), about USD 26.8bn at 7.8
markets: 17,114 stores in 31 markets across Asia and Europe, including China, Philippines, UK, Benelux, Germany and Poland
rationale: Owner of Watsons and Superdrug with a huge Asian and European shopper base; F1's beauty and lifestyle partners show the category fits.

name: Uniqlo
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Japanese casual-wear brand selling LifeWear clothing through about 2,500 stores in 26 countries and territories.
capacity_detail: Naming-rights partner of MLB's Los Angeles Dodgers ('UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium'), announced March 2026, reported five-year deal over USD 125M
sponsorships: Los Angeles Dodgers field naming rights (2026); global ambassadors Roger Federer (2018), Kei Nishikori (2011), Emma Raducanu (2026), Shingo Kunieda (2009)
markets: 2,499 stores: 782 in Japan and 1,717 abroad across Asia, North America and Europe
rationale: Global apparel brand investing heavily in elite sport ambassadors; F1 team kit or driver apparel would extend its sports credibility.

name: HK Express
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Hong Kong low-cost airline flying to about 27 destinations in Asia, wholly owned by Cathay Pacific.
capacity_detail: Revenue HK$6,778M in 2025 (Wikipedia business trends table), about USD 870M at 7.8
markets: Scheduled flights from Hong Kong to Japan, Korea, Southeast Asia and other Asian destinations
rationale: Budget airline targeting young Asian travellers; F1 race-trip packages to Japan, Shanghai and Singapore fit its network.

name: Peach Aviation
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Japanese low-cost airline flying domestic routes and short-haul Asian routes from Kansai and other hubs.
ownership: subsidiary of ANA Holdings (via All Nippon Airways), full ownership since December 2024
capacity_detail: Revenue JPY 139.3bn in year to March 2024 (Wikipedia financial table), about USD 930M at 150
markets: Japan domestic routes plus China, Hong Kong, Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Thailand
rationale: Leisure airline from Osaka could sell fan travel to the Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka, its natural catchment.

name: CJ Olive Young
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: South Korea's leading health and beauty store chain with over 1,300 stores, a global online mall and US stores.
capacity_detail: Standalone 2025 sales KRW 5.8335tn, up 21.8% (FSS filing as reported), about USD 4.2bn at 1,380
markets: South Korea stores, global online mall, Sephora shop-in-shops (2026) and first US store in Pasadena (May 2026)

signals.regions: Opened first US store in Pasadena, California (May 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olive_Young_(company))

rationale: K-beauty retailer expanding into the US; F1's young, growing female fanbase suits a brand building global awareness.

name: Supercheap Auto
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Australian and New Zealand retailer of car parts, accessories and tools, with 362 stores, owned by Super Retail Group.
capacity_detail: Segment sales A$1,591.6M in FY26 (year to June 2026, Super Retail Group results), about USD 1.03bn at 0.65
sponsorships: Bathurst 1000 naming rights 2005-2020; Supercars team sponsorships since 1997; TCR Australia naming rights from 2021; Triple Eight associate sponsor 2021-2025
markets: Australia and New Zealand, about 362 stores plus online
rationale: Car-enthusiast retailer with decades of Supercars sponsorship; an Australian Grand Prix or F1 team tie-in is a natural step up.

name: rebel
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Australia's leading sporting goods and apparel retailer, operating about 160 stores as part of Super Retail Group.
capacity_detail: Segment sales A$1,422.7M in FY26 (year to June 2026, Super Retail Group results), about USD 925M at 0.65
markets: Australia (stores and online), with a smaller New Zealand presence
rationale: Sports retailer selling team merchandise; F1 licensed apparel and Australian Grand Prix activations could drive traffic.

name: BCF
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Australian outdoor retailer (Boating Camping Fishing) selling camping, fishing and boating gear, owned by Super Retail Group.
capacity_detail: Segment sales A$952.7M in FY26 (year to June 2026, Super Retail Group results), about USD 620M at 0.65
markets: Australia, through stores and online
rationale: Outdoor-leisure retailer with a mostly male customer base; F1 fit is limited to a domestic Grand Prix activation.

name: FILA China
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Business selling FILA sportswear in mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao, run by Anta Sports since 2009.
ownership: brand business of Anta Sports, which acquired the FILA trademark for mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao in 2009
capacity_detail: FILA segment revenue RMB 28.47bn in 2025, up 6.9% (Anta results release), about USD 3.95bn at 7.2
markets: Mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao
rationale: Premium sport-fashion brand in China; F1's Shanghai race and lifestyle image suit FILA's upmarket positioning.

name: Hang Seng Bank
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Major Hong Kong retail and commercial bank, delisted in January 2026 after HSBC bought the remaining shares.
ownership: subsidiary of HSBC Holdings (62.14% before; 100% after privatisation, delisted 27 January 2026)
capacity_detail: Operating income HK$36,764M in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox), about USD 4.7bn at 7.8
markets: Hong Kong, with a mainland China subsidiary
rationale: Hong Kong's household-name bank; F1 hospitality could serve wealth clients, though spending is largely domestic.

name: Telkomsel
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Indonesia's largest mobile operator, serving about 156 million customers, owned 69.9% by Telkom Indonesia and 30.1% by Singtel.
ownership: subsidiary of Telkom Indonesia (69.9%); Singtel holds 30.1%
capacity_detail: Revenue Rp109.3tn in 2025 (detik report of Telkomsel results), about USD 6.8bn at 16,000
markets: Indonesia nationwide, about 156.1 million consolidated customers
rationale: Dominant Indonesian consumer brand with a young mobile audience; F1 streaming and esports content could deepen engagement.

name: Swire Coca-Cola
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Coca-Cola bottler serving 911 million people in Greater China, Taiwan, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand and Laos.
ownership: subsidiary of Swire Pacific (Beverages Division); Swire Pacific is controlled by John Swire & Sons
capacity_detail: Swire Coca-Cola revenue HK$41,976M in 2025 (Swire Pacific annual results), about USD 5.4bn at 7.8
markets: 11 Chinese provinces and Shanghai, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos and most of Thailand
rationale: Large bottler but it sells The Coca-Cola Company's brands; sponsorship decisions sit mostly with the brand owner.

name: Marina Bay Sands
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Singapore integrated resort with hotel, casino, convention centre, shopping and SkyPark, owned by Las Vegas Sands.
capacity_detail: Marina Bay Sands net revenues USD 5,590M for full year 2025 (LVS Q4 2025 earnings release)
markets: Singapore resort drawing tourists and high-value visitors from across Asia and beyond
rationale: Landmark resort beside the Marina Bay circuit; Singapore Grand Prix hospitality and title rights fit its premium, international guest base.

name: EnergyAustralia
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
industry: electricity and gas retailer and generator
desc: Australian energy retailer and generator supplying electricity and gas to over 1.7 million homes and businesses.
ownership: subsidiary of CLP Holdings (CLP Group's Australia segment)
capacity_detail: CLP Australia segment (EnergyAustralia) revenue HK$34,191M in 2025 (CLP annual results), about USD 4.4bn at 7.8
markets: Eastern Australian states, more than 1.7 million residential and business customers
rationale: Energy retailer fighting customer churn; Australian Grand Prix ties could support its EV charging and clean-energy messaging.

name: Samsung Display
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
industry: OLED and LCD display panel maker
desc: Maker of OLED and LCD display panels for smartphones, TVs, monitors and laptops, majority owned by Samsung Electronics.
ownership: subsidiary of Samsung Electronics (84.80%); Samsung SDI holds 15.20% (Sep 2022)
capacity_detail: Full-year 2025 revenue about KRW 29.9tn (about USD 23.0bn), the sum of Samsung's quarterly SDC segment disclosures (Display Daily)
markets: Supplies display panels to smartphone, TV, IT and automotive brands worldwide
rationale: Mainly a B2B component maker; F1 would serve technology showcasing to automotive cockpit-display customers rather than consumers.

name: Rakuten Mobile
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Japanese mobile carrier running a cloud-native network with about 10 million subscriptions, wholly owned by Rakuten Group.
capacity_detail: Revenue JPY 374.7bn in fiscal 2025, up about 32% (RCR Wireless report of Rakuten results), about USD 2.5bn at 150
markets: Japan, 10.01 million subscriptions at end of 2025
rationale: Challenger carrier chasing subscribers; it could activate its parent's Ferrari F1 deal around the Japanese Grand Prix.

name: Woowa Brothers (Baemin)
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
industry: food delivery and quick commerce app
desc: Operator of Baemin, South Korea's leading food delivery app, plus the B mart quick-commerce grocery service.
ownership: subsidiary of Delivery Hero via Woowa DH Asia (89.55%); founder Kim Bong-jin 8.36%
capacity_detail: Consolidated revenue KRW 5.283tn in 2025, up 22.2% (Digital Today report of earnings release), about USD 3.8bn at 1,380
markets: South Korea nationwide food delivery and grocery delivery
rationale: Consumer app brand in a fierce fight with Coupang Eats; F1's growing Korean fanbase could add premium brand heat.

name: Bach Hoa Xanh
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Vietnamese grocery and fresh-food store chain with nearly 3,000 stores, majority owned by Mobile World Investment.
ownership: subsidiary of Mobile World Investment via Bach Hoa Xanh Technology and Investment JSC (94.99%)
capacity_detail: 2025 revenue VND 46,900bn, up 14% (TCBS research report on MWG, June 2026), about USD 1.9bn at 25,000
markets: Vietnam, 2,962 stores as of April 2026

signals.ipo: IPO planned for 2028 per MWG roadmap (Jun 2026; https://www.tcbs.com.vn/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/MWG_Bao_cao_phan_tich_chi_tiet_EN-1.pdf)

rationale: Fast-growing Vietnamese grocer with an IPO ahead; little natural F1 fit beyond domestic brand building.

name: Airtel Money
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Mobile money and digital payments business of Airtel Africa, serving customers across its African markets.
ownership: subsidiary of Airtel Africa (Airtel Mobile Commerce B.V.); TPG's Rise Fund and Mastercard are minority shareholders; Airtel Africa is controlled by Bharti Airtel
capacity_detail: Mobile money revenue USD 1,355M in year to March 2026 (Airtel Africa final results)
markets: Airtel Africa's markets across East, Central and West Africa including Nigeria

signals.ipo: IPO intended in second half of 2026, London preferred (May 2026; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/airtel-africa--aaf/final-results/9558210)

rationale: Pan-African fintech heading for an IPO; global sports visibility could build investor and consumer awareness, as rival fintechs use F1.

name: Airtel Payments Bank
group: Subsidiaries of listed groups: Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
desc: Indian payments bank offering savings accounts, UPI payments and remittances through Airtel's retail network and app.
ownership: subsidiary of Bharti Airtel; 99.9% of equity held by Bharti Group companies (Dec 2021)
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 3,207 crore (about USD 340M) in FY26 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: India, through Airtel retail points and the Airtel Thanks app
rationale: Mass-market Indian payments bank; F1 offers little reach for its low-income customer base.
